title: pseudopanax ferox
intro: Pseudopanax ferox, commonly known as the lancewood or harakeke, is a plant species native to New Zealand, characterized by its evergreen foliage and unique, lance-shaped leaves. The lancewood has been used in traditional Maori medicine for various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which can aid in wound healing and reduce pain and swelling. The therapeutic actions of lancewood include its ability to stimulate digestion, improve circulation, and reduce stress and anxiety. The bioactive constituents of lancewood include lignans, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
